title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

deep.reconstruction:
Problem: a vertical heavy column AB of height b (axis AB vertical, top A, bottom B) is slightly bent in its plane. Its top A and foot B are held on the vertical line AB by horizontal reactions A and B. The foot carries the vertical reaction M, which equals the total weight. Each element dx carries the weight M dx/b. A uniform horizontal load C dx/b also acts on each element (forces YV). Coordinates are x = AX downward and deflection y = XY. Because the deflection is infinitesimal, arc length is identified with dx, and the centre of gravity G lies at horizontal distance g = GO = (1/b)∫y dx from the axis.

§16, global equilibrium. Horizontal forces: A + B = C. Vertical forces: M (up at B) and M (down at G) cancel. Moments about A: A and the reaction at B (which lies on the axis line) give zero moment. The reaction at B gives B·b, and the weight gives M·g, both in the same sense. The distributed horizontal load gives ∫_0^b (C/b) x dx = Cb/2 in the opposite sense. Hence Bb + Mg = Cb/2, so B = C/2 − Mg/b and A = C/2 + Mg/b.

§17 begins the local equilibrium. Imagine the column fixed at an arbitrary point Y and take moments about Y of all forces on the arc AY. Their sum must equal the elastic moment Ekk/r, where r is the radius of curvature (Euler–Bernoulli bending law). The moment of A about Y is A x. The next page computes the distributed-load contributions: C x²/(2b) from the horizontal loads and (M/b)∫(y−u)dt from the weights. Together these lead to an integro-differential equation for the heavy column, linearized with 1/r ≈ ±d²y/dx².
errors: No mathematical error on this page; the global statics are correct given the sign conventions Euler adopts.

Minor inconsistency carried over from the previous page: there the weight force Gg = M is called 'horizontalis', whereas here (correctly) it is treated as vertical. That is a slip in the original text.
The fixed vertical end reaction M at B together with the external weight is consistent only to first order in the deflection; this is standard linearization, acceptable for a buckling analysis.

ideas.what: Global force and moment equilibrium of a slightly bent heavy pinned column with a uniform lateral load, determining the end reactions A = C/2 + Mg/b and B = C/2 − Mg/b, where g is the centroid offset (1/b)∫y dx

ideas.what: Retaining the weight's eccentricity through the area integral ∫y dx (a nonlocal term) in the heavy-column equilibrium
